title: Expose stable quantization profile IDs + metadata in Model Catalog for Standard Cost Model
creator: Ethan Park
body:
Problem
Today the cost model, runtime telemetry, and Optimize prototypes refer to quantization in inconsistent ways (free-form strings like "int8", "gptq", "awq", or implicit execution-path IDs). This causes:
- Non-deterministic cost projections: the same model/config can be interpreted differently across Console vs Optimize.
- Fragile joins between telemetry (runtime execution path) and static model metadata.
- Migration pain: Console/Optimize cannot safely cache or reason about what changed when quantization settings evolve.

We need the Model Catalog to expose stable, canonical quantization profile identifiers and enough metadata for cost modeling to parameterize expected throughput/memory deltas and enforce guardrails.

Scope
Add quantization_profile_id (stable) + quantization profile metadata to Model Catalog responses and internal SDK types.
- Stable identifier must be usable as a key in:
  - Cost Model input schema (model characteristics)
  - Telemetry joins (execution path -> quant profile)
  - Optimize what-if inputs (requested quant profile)
- Metadata must be explicit and versioned enough that cost model behavior is deterministic.

Non-goals
- Choosing which quant profiles are "recommended" for a workload (Optimize owns that).
- Implementing the cost model math itself (ENG-4824).
- Customer-facing naming/marketing strings (this is internal canonicalization).

Proposed API changes (Model Catalog)
1) Add a stable ID field to each quantization profile:
- quantization_profile_id: string
  - Format: "qprof_<vendor?>_<family>_<bits>_<variant>_v<semver>" OR UUID-like; must be stable and human-diffable.
  - Recommendation: human-diffable with a semver suffix, e.g. "qprof_awq_w4a16_v1".
  - Once published, IDs must never be reused for different semantics.

2) Add structured metadata under the model version entry (exact response shape depends on catalog service conventions, but must include these semantic fields):
- quantization_method: enum-ish string (e.g., "none" | "awq" | "gptq" | "bitsandbytes" | "fp8")
- weight_bits: integer string (e.g., "4", "8", "16")
- activation_dtype: string (e.g., "fp16" | "bf16" | "fp8")
- kernel_path_id: string (maps to runtime execution path identifier; may be hardware-specific)
- memory_multiplier_vs_fp16: string float (e.g., "0.62")
- throughput_multiplier_vs_fp16_prefill: string float (e.g., "1.10")
- throughput_multiplier_vs_fp16_decode: string float (e.g., "1.25")
- quality_constraint_hint: string (free-form but bounded; e.g., "requires eval gate: legal_summarization_v2")
- notes: string (optional)

3) Backward compatibility
- Keep existing free-form fields (if present) but mark as deprecated in the SDK types + docs.
- Add a best-effort mapping from legacy strings -> quantization_profile_id (for older model entries) to avoid breaking callers.

ID governance + change policy
- ID ownership: Runtime Scheduling/Kernels (Grace Kim) in partnership with Applied ML (Arjun Desai) and Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park).
- Adding a new quant profile requires:
  - A new quantization_profile_id (never mutate semantics of an existing ID)
  - Runtime kernel_path_id wired to telemetry (or explicitly "unavailable")
  - A short metadata record with multipliers (even if initially "1.0" placeholders, but must be explicit)
- Updating multipliers without semantic changes should be done by bumping the semver suffix on the profile ID (preferred) OR introducing a separate metadata_version field (if catalog constraints require). Decision: prefer new ID with bumped version to keep joins deterministic across reporting windows.

Acceptance criteria
- Model Catalog API responses for all Redwood-verified models include quantization_profile_id for every supported quantization option.
- At least the top 10 most-used models (by token volume) have quant profiles fully populated with:
  - method, bits/dtype, kernel_path_id
  - multipliers split for prefill vs decode
- Cost Model schema v1 can reference quantization_profile_id as the canonical key without requiring free-form parsing.
- Telemetry can join runtime execution path -> kernel_path_id -> quantization_profile_id with documented fallbacks.
- Console/Optimize can cache cost model responses safely using quantization_profile_id as part of the cache key.

Implementation plan
1) Catalog schema + storage
- Extend catalog DB schema / config store to store quantization profiles as first-class entities with stable IDs.
- Add an internal migration that assigns IDs for existing profiles (deterministic mapping; document the mapping table).

2) API + SDK changes
- Extend internal Model Catalog protobuf/JSON response to include quantization_profile_id and metadata fields.
- Update shared SDK types used by cost-model service to read these fields.
- Add contract tests for:
  - presence of quantization_profile_id
  - stable serialization (no field renames without version bump)

3) Runtime/telemetry alignment hooks
- Confirm kernel_path_id values match runtime export identifiers (see runtime metrics contract work).
- If a profile is supported by catalog but runtime doesn’t yet export a stable kernel path, mark kernel_path_id as "unknown" and block enabling it for Optimize what-if until available.

4) Rollout
- Stage behind a catalog response version header if needed (e.g., X-Redwood-Catalog-Version: 2026-02-quantprofiles).
- Verify no callers break (Console/Optimize reading only known fields).

References / links
- Confluence: applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-cost-modeling-notes.json
- Linear: ENG-4822 (schema v1), ENG-4824 (what-if), ENG-4828 (runtime kv/cache metrics)
- GitHub (tracking): sources/github/redwood/pr-28502-model-catalog-quant-profile-identifiers.json

Open questions
- Do we need hardware-specific variants as separate quantization_profile_id (e.g., H100 fp8 kernels vs A100)? Current proposal: yes—if the runtime behavior differs materially and would change cost multipliers, use distinct IDs.
- Do we store multipliers per hardware SKU rather than globally? Initial v1: single set of multipliers + allow cost model to override based on runtime benchmarks; v2 may require per-SKU tables.

Risks
- ID churn: if teams treat IDs as mutable labels, joins will break across reporting windows. Mitigation: enforce “never reuse ID for different semantics” and prefer new IDs for multiplier changes.
- Missing/incorrect multipliers: can cause Optimizer ROI inflation. Mitigation: explicit placeholders + confidence flags handled at cost model layer; this ticket ensures metadata is explicit and versioned.

Testing
- Add golden fixtures for a small set of models showing:
  - unquantized baseline ("none")
  - w8a16 profile
  - w4a16 profile
- Add a join test: runtime kernel_path_id -> quantization_profile_id resolves for fixtures.
comments: 2026-01-22 (Arjun Desai): Strong +1. Please ensure we can represent uncertainty/quality gating separately from the ID. ID should represent the execution semantics only; quality constraints can be hints.
2026-01-24 (Sofia Ivanova): For batching/throughput modeling we need prefill/decode multipliers separately. Decode gains can be much larger; please don’t compress to one number.

2026-01-28 (Ethan Park): Aligning on ID policy: treat quant_profile_id as immutable. If any multiplier changes meaningfully, create a new ID with bumped suffix; do not mutate existing record in-place.
2026-02-03 (Grace Kim): Implemented catalog schema extension and response fields in a draft PR. Next: backfill IDs for existing profiles; need applied-ml signoff on mapping table.
2026-02-06 (Nadia Rahman): Please include kernel_path_id in catalog; telemetry join needs to be stable and not derived from model name strings.
2026-02-10 (Grace Kim): Backfill script assigns IDs deterministically: method+weight_bits+activation_dtype+variant -> qprof_<...>_v1. Added contract tests for presence + stability.

2026-02-12 (Chloe Martin): Console use-case: we will use quantization_profile_id in cache keys for cost breakdown queries. Please confirm IDs won’t change between deployments for the same model version.

2026-02-14 (Grace Kim): Confirmed policy: IDs immutable; new semantics => new ID. For same model version we will not rewrite IDs retroactively; changes will land as additional profiles or a new model version entry.
2026-02-21 (Benji Okafor): Reviewed API compatibility: adding fields only, no breaking changes. Please document deprecated legacy fields and expected mapping behavior in catalog docs.

2026-02-28 (Grace Kim): Landed via PR pr-28502-model-catalog-quant-profile-identifiers. Follow-up: cost-model service to consume quant_profile_id (ENG-4824) and add validation harness fixtures (ENG-4831).
